record.summary: OMB memorandum directing federal agencies to strengthen AI governance, advance responsible AI innovation and manage risks from their use of AI. Each agency had to designate a Chief AI Officer within 60 days, and CFO Act agencies had to develop AI strategies. By 1 December 2024 agencies had to apply minimum risk-management practices to safety-impacting and rights-impacting AI, including an AI impact assessment, real-world testing, independent evaluation, ongoing monitoring, operator training and human oversight, and public notice, plus notice to negatively affected individuals and opt-out options for rights-impacting AI, or else stop using the AI.
record.notes: Issued on 28 March 2024 consistent with the AI in Government Act of 2020, the Advancing American AI Act and Executive Order 14110, after a draft published for public comment on 1 November 2023. It governs only agencies' own use of AI and does not create rights or obligations for the public; Sections 5(a) to 5(c) do not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community. Rescinded and replaced on 3 April 2025 by OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (US-12), issued after Executive Order 14179 of 23 January 2025. Its companion acquisition memorandum M-24-18 was likewise rescinded and replaced by M-25-22 of the same day.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the M-24-10 PDF stored on 11 Oct 2026 from the NARA-archived Biden White House site (bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov could not be resolved from the archiver's machine on 17 Oct 2026). It confirms the memo number, title, 28 Mar 2024 date, the CAIO and 1 Dec 2024 deadlines and the minimum practices. M-25-21 and M-25-22 (whitehouse.gov) were stored in this run: M-25-21 of 3 Apr 2025 rescinds and replaces M-24-10 (status, date_last_updated), and M-25-22 of the same day rescinds and replaces M-24-18. Version 1's 'First binding government-wide policy', the EO 14179 section number and the October 2024 date of M-24-18 rest on no stored file and were removed.

title.quote: SUBJECT: Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence

legal_force.quote: all agencies are required to implement minimum practices, detailed below, to manage risks from safety-impacting AI

summary.quote: each agency must designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) within 60 days of the date of the issuance of this memorandum.
This memorandum requires each agency identified in the Chief Financial Officers Act (CFO Act)4 to develop an enterprise strategy for how they will advance the responsible use of AI.

By December 1, 2024, agencies must implement the minimum practices in Section 5(c) of this memorandum for safety-impacting and rights-impacting AI, or else stop using any AI in their operations that is not compliant with the minimum practices
A. Complete an AI impact assessment.
B. Test the AI for performance in a real-world context.
G. Ensure adequate human training and assessment.
I. Provide public notice and plain-language documentation.
F. Maintain options to opt-out for AI-enabled decisions.

notes.quote: This memorandum accounts for public comments that OMB received following its publication of a draft version of this memorandum on November 1, 2023.
Consistent with the AI in Government Act of 2020,1 the Advancing American AI Act,2 and Executive Order 14110 on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
this memorandum governs only agencies’ own use of AI and does not create rights or obligations for the public
However, Section 5(a) through (c) of this memorandum do not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community.
This memorandum rescinds and replaces Office of Management and Budget (0MB) Memorandum M-24-10, Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use ofArtificial Intelligence.
